subject: OWNER DECISION: same family for both council voices (temporary)
directive:
Owner decision 2026-10-09, superseding the blocked-by-default consequence of c6ab55e. For now the council runs BOTH voices on the same family it already uses: chair on opencode-acct-5 (role reason), challenger/reviewer on new-provider (role review), both model space-bunny-free. Routing is being repaired, so a genuine second family is not available right now. This is an EXPLICIT OWNER EXCEPTION, not a weakening of the quorum law. What you must do:
(1) Keep c6ab55e's definition intact and visible: quorum is two distinct MODEL families. Record this decision as an owner-granted exception with its date and its reason (routing repair in progress), not as a rule change.
(2) Change the OUTCOME, not the definition: a convening with two answering voices now produces a ruling, labelled: quorum: OWNER-EXCEPTION (single family, space-bunny) - not independently corroborated. Confidence labels stay honest: no ruling may be labelled 'multi-model' or claim independence; cap default confidence at low and state plainly that two copies of one model agreeing is not independent corroboration.
(3) Name every place this changes behaviour (the quorum section, the circuit-breaker text for QUORUM-LOSS, the saved workflow, the route-line template) and update all of them consistently, then state which files you edited.
(4) Add the expiry condition: this exception lapses automatically the moment routing is repaired and a second family is available. Record it as OPEN with the condition 'routing repaired and second family live' so it cannot quietly become permanent.
(5) Keep the breaker: if fewer than two voices ANSWER, still BLOCK with QUORUM-LOSS. The exception relaxes the family requirement only, never the requirement that two voices reply.
Do not weaken any Ratchet gate, do not touch product code, do not push. Reply DONE with the edited files, the exact new wording, and the recorded expiry condition.
